shared:
The Mist Lynx is a 25-ton Clan OmniMech designed by Clan Smoke Jaguar in 2926 to serve as a fast, agile light scout and raider. Designated "Koshi," meaning "small death," by Draconis Combine forces who first encountered the design during Operation REVIVAL, the Mist Lynx quickly earned a reputation for punishing enemies who underestimated its capabilities. The design proved so successful that it spread through Trials of Possession to the touman of every Clan within a generation of its introduction, becoming one of the most ubiquitous light OmniMechs in Clan service.

Despite its age and the introduction of newer light OmniMechs, the fundamental soundness of the Mist Lynx has kept it in continuous production across multiple Clan manufacturers for over a century. Its unmatched combination of speed, jump capability, and electronic warfare potential ensures that the design remains a valued asset in any Clan touman.

The Mist Lynx is built on a lightweight Light Series II endo steel chassis powered by a Type II 175 XL engine, propelling the twenty-five-ton OmniMech to speeds approaching 119 kilometers per hour. Six jump jets provide an impressive 180-meter jump capability, granting the design exceptional tactical flexibility across varied terrain. Only the Grendel and Dragonfly among standard OmniMech configurations can match this combination of speed and agility. A permanently mounted active probe allows the Mist Lynx to detect hidden units before they can spring an ambush, making it a natural choice for reconnaissance operations and screening duties.

This fixed equipment, combined with the endo steel frame and ferro-fibrous armor, comes at a significant cost to offensive capability. The Mist Lynx has only seven and a half tons of available pod space, among the lowest of any Clan OmniMech. Armor protection is particularly thin at just three and a half tons of Compound H17 ferro-fibrous plating, making the design extremely vulnerable to concentrated fire. In its Prime configuration, the 'Mech carries an LRM-10 for ranged engagement, a Streak SRM-4 for close combat, and a pair of machine guns for anti-infantry work. The Mist Lynx's true strength lies not in any single weapons loadout but in its nearly unmatched maneuverability, which allows skilled MechWarriors to dictate engagement terms against heavier opponents.

The Mist Lynx was developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar scientists during the early decades of the thirtieth century, emerging as a dedicated light scout designed to exploit OmniMech technology at the lightest practical weight class. The design quickly proved popular, and through Trials of Possession and political exchanges, the Mist Lynx spread to virtually every Clan's touman within a generation of its introduction.

During Operation REVIVAL in 3049, Draconis Combine forces encountered the Mist Lynx extensively across multiple invasion corridors. The design earned its Inner Sphere reporting name "Koshi" from DCMS intelligence analysts, a term reflecting the 'Mech's ability to inflict disproportionate damage through hit-and-run tactics. Clan Smoke Jaguar fielded the largest concentration of Mist Lynxes during the invasion, though the design appeared in nearly every invading Clan's order of battle.

The Annihilation of Clan Smoke Jaguar following Operation BULLDOG and the Great Refusal in 3060 disrupted primary production at the Huntress Production Facility Epsilon. Clans Ice Hellion and Steel Viper both took advantage of the SLDF's invasion of Huntress to trial for the right to manufacture the light OmniMech, bringing it back into production before the Wars of Reaving. The Steel Vipers secured ongoing production at the Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-O3, while the Ice Hellions maintained output from Huntress.

The Wars of Reaving in 3070 brought further turmoil to Mist Lynx production lines. During the conflict, Steel Viper forces employed Mist Lynxes in rapid flanking actions during the seizure of Lum, where a Binary of the light OmniMechs outmaneuvered Snow Raven auxiliaries attempting to intervene. The subsequent destruction of Clan Steel Viper and the absorption of Clan Ice Hellion further redistributed production facilities among the surviving Clans.

During the ilClan era, the Mist Lynx continued to demonstrate its enduring tactical value. As Clan Wolf marched toward Terra, Mist Lynxes of the Ninth Wolf Guard Striker Cluster provided essential reconnaissance on Alula Australis, foiling multiple Republic headhunter attempts targeting senior Clan officers. The design's presence across centuries of conflict and political upheaval speaks to both its fundamental soundness and the widespread industrial capacity dedicated to its continued manufacture.

shared: The Nova, designated Black Hawk by Inner Sphere forces, was among the earliest OmniMechs ever produced when it first rolled off the assembly lines at Tokasha MechWorks in 2870. Designed by Clan Hell's Horses as an infantry support platform, the Nova holds the distinction of being the first OmniMech specifically engineered with connection points allowing Elemental battle armor to mount and dismount the chassis with ease, a feature that would become standard across all subsequent Clan OmniMech designs. Produced by a limited number of facilities over its long service life, the Nova has nonetheless spread to every Clan through trials and salvage, earning a reputation as one of the most versatile and recognizable medium OmniMechs in the Kerensky Cluster and beyond.

The Nova is built around a 250 XL Model SF-2 extralight engine that propels the fifty-ton chassis to a top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Five jump jets provide exceptional maneuverability with a jumping distance of one hundred and fifty meters, allowing the Nova to exploit terrain that would stymie heavier opponents. The design carries ten tons of Forge Type HH30 armor, providing ninety-six percent of maximum protection for its weight class, a generous allocation that reflects the Hell's Horses' emphasis on survivability in combined-arms operations.

The chassis dedicates sixteen tons to pod space, enabling a wide range of configurations. In its Primary configuration, the Nova mounts twelve extended-range medium lasers distributed across both arms, creating a devastating close-range barrage capable of shredding battle armor and light vehicles in seconds. However, this firepower comes at a steep cost in waste heat. Even with eighteen double heat sinks, the Nova Prime generates nearly twice as much heat as it can dissipate during a full alpha strike, forcing MechWarriors to carefully manage their fire discipline or risk emergency shutdowns.

The weaknesses of the Nova's design become apparent across its various configurations. The limited pod tonnage constrains heavier weapon loads, and configurations mounting ballistic weapons like the B and C variants often sacrifice secondary armament. Even so, the combination of speed, jump capability, and configuration flexibility has made the Nova one of the most versatile medium OmniMechs ever fielded.

The Nova made its battlefield debut in 2872 during the combined assault on Kindraa Smythe-Jewel on Foster, launched by the Hell's Horses alongside Clan Coyote and Kindraa Payne. The attack proved devastatingly effective, wiping out the Smythe-Jewels as a faction and establishing the Nova as a proven combat design. The Hell's Horses' new mechanized battle armor tactics, enabled by the Nova's Elemental mounting points, proved so successful that the concept became standard on all subsequent OmniMechs.

Originally manufactured at a single facility on Tokasha, production ceased in 2921 when Clan Ghost Bear captured the world during the Battle of Tokasha, after which the facility produced only spare parts. Every Clan acquired examples through trials and salvage over the following centuries, ensuring the design remained ubiquitous if increasingly scarce. The Nova's versatility as a jack of all trades saw it deployed across every major Clan conflict of the Golden Century and beyond, though it was increasingly relegated to a secondary role as heavier and lighter OmniMechs entered service.

The Clan Invasion of the Inner Sphere in 3049 brought the Nova to the attention of the Great Houses, where it earned the reporting name Black Hawk. Inner Sphere encounters with the design directly inspired the Draconis Combine's Black Hawk-KU program and later the Penetrator developed by Kallon Industries. The Nova's balanced design proved so influential that it spawned an entire lineage of derivative designs across both Clan and Inner Sphere production lines.

Clan Jade Falcon resurrected Nova production at Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten in 3073, over two hundred years after the original lines fell silent, breathing new life into the aging design. The Falcons fielded Novas extensively during their campaigns in the mid-thirty-second century, including the invasion of Arc-Royal in 3146, where a Star of Novas from the Fifty-Third Falcon Talon intercepted elements of the First Wolf Legion Cluster screening the evacuation of the Exiled Wolf leadership. The Novas' varied configurations caused confusion among the defenders, enabling the Falcon Trinary to press their advantage.

Meanwhile, Clan Hell's Horses maintained a especially large concentration of Novas in their touman, and in the mid-3140s numerous examples found their way into the Hell's Horses forces during the Golden Ordun alliance. The last Nova production facility in the Clan Homeworlds, on Sheridan under Clan Star Adder control, was eventually retooled to produce Pouncers by 3087, leaving the few remaining Homeworld examples in the hands of Aggressor MechWarriors operating on the fringes of Clan society.

The OmniMarauder was born from a 3135 General Motors feasibility study conducted at their Kathil facility, exploring the future potential of the iconic Marauder chassis. Rather than simply upgrading the existing design, the project took the radical step of reimagining the venerable heavy 'Mech as a mixed-technology OmniMech, incorporating extensive Clan-grade components into an Inner Sphere frame. The design effort drew upon outside expertise from Bander BattleMechs, reflecting the collaborative nature of the ambitious undertaking.

The resulting prototype demonstrated remarkable capability but at a prohibitive cost, ensuring the design remained an individual prototype rather than entering mass production. The OmniMarauder serves primarily as a technology demonstrator for what the Marauder platform could become when freed from the constraints of production economics.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration N transforms the Mist Lynx into a dedicated long-range missile platform. Four LRM-5 launchers, two per arm, provide sustained indirect fire capability, though all four launchers share a single ton of ammunition that limits endurance to approximately six volleys. A TAG laser designator in the right torso allows the pilot to spot for its own missiles or guide fire from Starmates equipped with semi-guided munitions. A laser anti-missile system provides defense against return missile fire, while a single heavy small laser offers limited fallback capability when ammunition runs dry. The N configuration is best employed in fire support Stars where its TAG capability and indirect fire complement heavier missile platforms.

Alternate Configuration P is designed for extreme close-quarters combat, particularly in urban environments. An ER large laser provides the only ranged capability, while the bulk of the pod space is devoted to an array of four ER micro lasers and three micro pulse lasers optimized for point-blank engagements. The micro pulse lasers are particularly effective in the confined spaces of city fighting, where their accuracy bonus at short range compensates for their limited reach. On open terrain, however, the P configuration's arsenal leaves the Mist Lynx severely disadvantaged, forced to close through killing fields of enemy fire before its primary weapons can bear. The P is best employed in dense terrain where engagement ranges are naturally compressed.

This variant configuration represents the Mist Lynx's most versatile standard loadout, equipping the 'Mech for a range of light combat duties. An LRM-10 provides meaningful ranged fire support capability, while a Streak SRM-4 offers efficient close-range punch with its lock-on technology eliminating wasted ammunition. Two machine guns round out the weapons suite with effective anti-infantry capability. This balanced configuration allows this variant to serve as a credible threat at multiple engagement ranges while fulfilling its primary reconnaissance role, though the light ammunition stores demand careful fire discipline during extended operations.

Alternate Configuration T is a Tiburon Khanate refresh of the classic Prime configuration, offering a modernized take on the original loadout. An LRM-10 with one ton of ammunition provides ranged fire support from the left arm, while a conventional SRM-4 with two ER small lasers occupies the right arm. The key improvements over the Prime are the addition of an ECM suite in the right torso and a secondary active probe in the head, significantly enhancing the 'Mech's electronic warfare and detection capabilities beyond the chassis's already formidable sensor suite. This electronic focus makes the T configuration arguably the most capable reconnaissance variant of the Mist Lynx, combining meaningful combat power with exceptional battlefield awareness.

Alternate Configuration Z was developed exclusively by The Society for use by its MechWarrior operatives. Built around a Nova CEWS electronic warfare system and supplementary active probe, the Z configuration prioritizes information warfare and battlefield coordination over direct combat. One ton of modular armor in the right torso provides additional protection for the sensitive Nova CEWS equipment. Armament is limited to a pair of iATM-3 launchers, one in each arm, providing modest firepower through improved advanced tactical missiles. The Z configuration saw limited deployment during the Wars of Reaving, used by Society operatives and their Dark Caste supporters in clandestine operations against mainstream Clan forces.

text.overview:
First seen among Clan Diamond Shark forces during the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052, the Mongrel was developed as a fast-moving medium OmniMech capable of leading strike and reconnaissance Stars deep behind enemy lines. The design proved itself admirably during the otherwise disastrous Shark campaign, where its speed and ammo-efficient weaponry allowed it to range far afield while simplifying resupply. Com Guard troops gave it the reporting name Grendel, and following a slight physical remodel the design entered full production in 3053.

One of the few successes of the Diamond Shark campaign, the Grendel immediately became the target of Trials of Possession from the other Invading Clans. Rather than expend warrior resources, the Sharks leveraged their merchant caste to negotiate production run sales and licensing agreements, ensuring the Grendel spread rapidly across multiple Clan front-line formations. Production has continued through the Dark Age era, with Clan Sea Fox maintaining the largest share of output.
text.capabilities:
Built around a powerful Consolidated 315 XL engine, the Grendel achieves a top speed of nearly 119 km/h, making it one of the fastest medium OmniMechs in service. Seven jump jets fixed to the chassis provide an impressive 210-meter leap capacity, granting pilots exceptional tactical flexibility in broken terrain. This combination of speed and agility allows the Grendel to dictate engagement ranges against most Inner Sphere opponents of similar tonnage, though the advantage proves less decisive in formal zellbrigen duels.

The Sharks employed endo steel internal structure and seven and a half tons of ferro-fibrous armor to maximize the thirteen and a half tons of available pod space. While the armor protection is adequate for a chassis of its weight, the Grendel relies on mobility rather than protection for survivability. The Prime configuration exemplifies the design philosophy, pairing an ER large laser for long-range engagement with three ER medium lasers and a Streak SRM-6 for devastating close-range firepower.

The Grendel has also earned a reputation for mechanical reliability unusual among OmniMechs. Where many OmniMech designs require frequent maintenance and are sometimes derisively called "hangar queens," the Grendel can operate for extended periods without significant technical attention, making it popular with technician castes across multiple Clans.
text.deployment: The Tiburon Khanate configuration stands as a modern refresh of the classic Prime loadout, optimized for close-range aggression. A large pulse laser and improved heavy small laser in the right arm provide devastating accuracy at short range, supported by a right torso-mounted SRM-6 rack. An ER small laser in the head provides supplementary fire, while twin improved heavy medium lasers in the left arm deliver punishing damage in close engagements. An extra double heat sink and a ton of SRM ammunition round out the configuration. This loadout reflects the Tiburon Khanate's preference for aggressive, close-range engagement doctrines.
text.battleHistory:
The Grendel's origins trace to a Clan Diamond Shark development program that bore fruit just in time for the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052. Originally designated the Mongrel, the design saw its combat debut leading light Stars on deep reconnaissance and raiding missions during the Shark campaign. While Clan Diamond Shark suffered a decisive defeat on the ComStar fortress world, the Mongrel's performance stood as one of the few unqualified successes of the engagement. The design was rechristened the Grendel after Com Guard troops applied the reporting name, and following minor physical modifications, it entered full production in 3053.

The other Invading Clans recognized the Grendel's potential almost immediately, staging numerous Trials of Possession for the design. In a move characteristic of their mercantile nature, the Diamond Sharks chose not to waste warrior resources defending against the flood of Trials. Instead, their merchant caste negotiated a series of agreements granting transportation rights, resources, material, and land in exchange for production run percentages and, in some cases, the design blueprints themselves. This shrewd approach accelerated the Sharks' post-Tukayyid recovery while ensuring the Grendel became a common sight among several Clan front-line toumans.

Production of the Grendel spread across multiple facilities, with the primary line at Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-T15 on Arcadia eventually being supplemented by additional manufacturing on Vinton and Alnabog in the Chain Cluster. During the Wars of Reaving, the Homeworld-based production on Vinton was disrupted, but the design's foothold in the Inner Sphere Clan occupation zones ensured its continued availability. Clan Hell's Horses in particular adopted the Grendel enthusiastically, finding it well-suited to their combined-arms doctrine.

In the Dark Age era, the Grendel remains a valued asset across the Inner Sphere Clans, though the majority of production has concentrated within the Clan Sea Fox Khanates. With Sea Fox merchants active among all the Great Houses and Clan Occupation Zones, the Grendel can be found in service across a wide swath of the Inner Sphere. A notable engagement in 3146 saw Tiburon Khanate forces employing Grendels during an independent raid against the Capellan world of Poznan, where a mixed striker Star of Grendels and Hellion OmniMechs overwhelmed a Home Guard company in a Trial of Possession for titanium ore, demonstrating the design's continued effectiveness well over a century after its introduction.

text.overview: The Nightstar was born in 2767 during the Amaris Civil War, commissioned by the Star League Defense Force after battlefield analysis revealed that unit commanders (particularly those piloting Marauder BattleMechs) were being systematically targeted by Amaris loyalist forces. Designed jointly by General Motors and Norse-Storm Technologies as a ninety-five-ton heavy support and command platform, the Nightstar entered production just eight months after its initial commission, a reflection of the urgency of the SLDF's need. The design saw distinguished service during the liberation of Terra before becoming an early casualty of the technological regression that followed the Star League's collapse. It would take nearly three centuries before the Federated Commonwealth restored the Nightstar to active production, returning one of the Star League's most formidable assault 'Mechs to the battlefield.
text.capabilities:
The Nightstar shares a number of design features with its Marauder lineage, but at twenty tons heavier and powered by a Pitban 285-rated extralight fusion engine, the chassis carries over fifty tons of weapons and equipment atop eighteen tons of Kallon Royalstar heavy armor. This combination of firepower and protection makes the Nightstar one of the most dangerous stand-off combatants in the Inner Sphere, capable of engaging and destroying opponents at virtually any range bracket.

The primary armament consists of twin Norse-Storm Model 7D Gauss rifles mounted in each arm, backed by a Defiance 1001 extended-range PPC in the right torso. This trio of weapons delivers devastating long-range firepower, with each Gauss rifle capable of stripping nearly a ton of armor per shot. For close-range defense, a pair of Defiance P5M medium pulse lasers and a head-mounted ExoStar small laser provide supplemental firepower. Fourteen double heat sinks manage the thermal load with minimal difficulty.

Beyond its weapons array, the Nightstar's electronics suite is exceptional. The Tek BattleCom communications system provides superior command-and-control capability, while the DLK Phased Array Sensor System (widely regarded as the finest stock targeting and tracking system available prior to the development of dedicated targeting computers) grants pilots extraordinary accuracy. This combination of firepower, protection, and sophisticated electronics firmly establishes the Nightstar's role as a premier command assault 'Mech, though its modest top speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour leaves it vulnerable to faster opponents that can dictate engagement range.
text.deployment: This heavily customized Nightstar features a comprehensive Clan-technology weapons refit combined with several unique additions. The primary armament retains twin Clan Gauss rifles fed from a combined four tons of ammunition, supported by a Clan ER PPC in the right torso and a Clan large pulse laser in the left torso, with a Clan ER small laser mounted in the head. Jump jets have been added to increase the 'Mech's mobility, while an Angel ECM Suite provides protection against advanced electronic warfare systems. Perhaps most especially, Triple Strength Myomer enhances both the 'Mech's speed and physical combat capability when operating at elevated temperatures, giving this Nightstar a unique tactical profile that combines long-range precision with surprising close-quarters effectiveness.
text.battleHistory:
The Nightstar's origins trace directly to the chaos of the Amaris Civil War, when Stefan Amaris's forces made a deliberate practice of targeting SLDF unit commanders in their distinctive Marauder BattleMechs. The SLDF's response was swift, within eight months of commissioning, the first Nightstars rolled off production lines at General Motors on Kathil and Norse Technologies on Afleir, providing commanders with a vastly more survivable platform from which to lead their forces. The design saw distinguished service during the liberation of Terra and the final campaigns against Amaris.

The Nightstar became one of the earliest victims of the First Succession War. In 2786, a Free Worlds League raid savaged the Norse Technologies factory on Afleir, while a freak accident killed the General Motors engineering team on Kathil. With both production lines silenced and the technological expertise to rebuild them lost, the Nightstar joined the growing list of Star League designs that slipped beyond the Inner Sphere's ability to manufacture. Surviving examples became increasingly rare prizes, fought over by Successor State militaries desperate for any edge.

Nearly three centuries later, in 3057, the recovery of lostech and advances in manufacturing enabled both halves of the fracturing Federated Commonwealth to restart Nightstar production. General Motors reopened its Kathil line, while Norse-Storm Technologies (the corporate successor to Norse Technologies) established production on Solaris VII. The timing proved fortuitous, as the Nightstar entered service just as the Clan threat and internal divisions within the Federated Commonwealth created enormous demand for heavy assault platforms.

During the FedCom Civil War, the Nightstar served on both sides of the conflict, with its presence on the battlefield often marking the location of senior commanders. Reports from the war include accounts of Nightstar pilots employing extreme measures in the bitter fighting (including the use of atomic weapons on worlds such as Axton and Marlette) illustrating the desperate intensity of that conflict. The Lyran Alliance permitted mercenary sales early on, particularly to units deployed along the Clan Occupation Zones, while the Federated Suns restricted sales to its most trusted mercenary commands only after line units like the Davion Assault Guards received adequate numbers.

The design has continued to see active production and deployment through the Jihad and into the Dark Age. General Motors leveraged its experience with the successful Marauder MAD-9D to restart an updated Nightstar production line on Kathil, producing the NSR-10D variant beginning around 3144. The Nightstar remains a symbol of battlefield command authority, its distinctive silhouette marking the presence of senior officers and elite formations across the Inner Sphere.

text.overview: The No-Dachi is a seventy-ton heavy BattleMech introduced in 3058 by the Cosby BattleMech Research Firm on Vega as the Draconis Combine's answer to the growing proliferation of melee-equipped BattleMechs fielded by the Federated Commonwealth. Named for the legendary oversized Japanese sword, the No-Dachi was designed to pair devastating close-combat capability with respectable ranged firepower. The samurai culture deeply ingrained in Combine MechWarriors made them resistant to the hatchets favored by Commonwealth designs, and the No-Dachi's sword offered a more elegant melee weapon befitting the Combine's warrior traditions. The design quickly became a fixture of frontline DCMS formations and remains in production well into the ilClan era.
text.capabilities:
The No-Dachi is built around its seven-meter katana-style sword, a weapon made truly devastating by the 'Mech's Triple Strength Myomer system. When running hot, the myomers dramatically increase the No-Dachi's striking power and boost its speed from 86 to 97 kilometers per hour, making it a fearsome opponent in close quarters. This heat dependency shapes the entire combat philosophy of the design, as pilots must carefully manage their thermal output to maximize myomer performance.

At range, the Lord's Light 2 extended-range PPC provides the primary long-range striking power, capable of softening targets as the No-Dachi closes the distance. The dual Shigunga MRM-20 racks deliver devastating medium-range barrages, though their inherent inaccuracy stands in stark contrast to the precision of the katana. A Guided Technologies SRM-2, Telos-4 SRM-4, and Diverse Optics medium laser round out the close-range arsenal, providing supplementary firepower and crucial heat generation to activate the myomers.

Riding on a Magna 350 XL engine, the No-Dachi achieves respectable speed for a seventy-ton design, though the extra-light engine's vulnerability to side torso hits is a significant weakness. Starshield A armor provides adequate protection, but pilots must be mindful that sustained exchanges of fire can expose the design's limitations before it reaches melee range.
text.deployment: Introduced in 3060, the 2KO represents the ultimate expression of the No-Dachi's close-combat philosophy. Removing the MRM launchers entirely and replacing the ER large laser with a large pulse laser, this variant mounts an array of pulse and ER lasers across multiple locations, supplemented by a flamer and three additional double heat sinks. Enhanced rear armor and a pair of ER medium lasers provide improved all-around protection and firepower when surrounded, making the 2KO particularly effective in chaotic melee engagements where threats come from every direction.
text.battleHistory:
The No-Dachi's development traces back to the mid-3050s, when the Cosby Myomer Research Firm (then primarily a myomer component supplier) partnered with the Eleventh Legion of Vega to develop a new close-combat BattleMech. The Legion, known for its technical expertise and its famous former commander Theodore Kurita, provided Cosby with advanced technologies and research support. In exchange, Cosby agreed to allocate half of all No-Dachi production to the Legion's ranks.

The design entered service in 3058 and quickly became synonymous with the Legion of Vega. Through special arrangement with Cosby, the bulk of No-Dachis were assigned to the Eleventh Legion, though several battalions' worth were distributed to other front-line DCMS units by the time of the FedCom Civil War. The design's association with the Legion proved a double-edged sword; Sword of Light regiments and other prestigious formations largely avoided the No-Dachi, preferring to lobby for a melee-capable 'Mech untainted by the Legion's reputation.

When the Word of Blake launched its invasion of Vega during the Jihad, the Draconis Combine ordered Cosby to relocate its production facilities deeper into the Combine. The company moved to Kajikazawa in the Benjamin Military District, an impressive logistical feat accomplished during wartime. By 3079, production lines were running at capacity, though a shortage of shipping infrastructure on the formerly backwater world initially hampered distribution. The bulk of output during this period went to the Second Benjamin Regulars tasked with defending Kajikazawa and the company's facilities.

The relocation proved fortuitous, as the Kajikazawa facility received significant government funding to develop experimental technologies, ultimately producing the NDA-3X prototype. The No-Dachi's prominence continued into the Dark Age, with senior DCMS commanders continuing to favor the design for frontline service. The Kajikazawa facility remained active through the ilClan era, producing updated variants including the NDA-3S Lyran export model, ensuring the No-Dachi's continued service across multiple factions and eras.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A reconfigures the Nova as a long-range sniper platform, mounting a pair of powerful extended-range particle projection cannons. A single medium pulse laser provides close-range defense, while twin anti-missile systems offer protection against incoming missile salvos. This configuration addresses one of the Prime's key weaknesses by enabling the Nova to engage effectively at extended ranges, though at the cost of the devastating close-range firepower that defines the chassis.

Alternate Configuration B pairs an Ultra Autocannon/5 capable of double-rate fire with a highly accurate large pulse laser, creating a versatile long-range engagement package. An extended-range small laser and two machine guns round out the armament for close encounters and anti-infantry work. The reliance on ammunition for the autocannon introduces a logistical dependency absent from the energy-heavy Prime, but the B configuration's balanced firepower makes it effective across multiple engagement ranges.

Alternate Configuration C centers its firepower around a single Gauss rifle, providing the Nova with devastating long-range striking power capable of crippling opponents before they can close to effective range. A small pulse laser and an SRM-4 launcher provide limited close-range defense. The Gauss rifle's lack of heat generation is a notable advantage on the heat-challenged Nova chassis, though the configuration's dependence on a single primary weapon creates vulnerability if that system is damaged.

Alternate Configuration D serves as a dedicated fire support platform, mounting an LRM-20 launcher for long-range direct and indirect bombardment alongside an LB 5-X autocannon that can fire cluster or slug rounds. This combination enables the Nova to function as both an artillery asset and a vehicle hunter, with the LB-X's cluster munitions proving particularly effective in an anti-aircraft role. The configuration sacrifices close-range lethality for sustained standoff engagement capability.

Introduced by Clan Coyote, Alternate Configuration E mounts a powerful ATM-12 launcher capable of firing ammunition optimized for short, medium, or long ranges, providing exceptional tactical flexibility. Three extended-range medium lasers supplement the missile system for close-range engagements. The ATM system's versatility partially addresses the Nova's characteristic weakness of limited pod tonnage, though the secondary armament remains modest compared to the Prime's devastating laser arrays.

Developed by Clan Hell's Horses as an experimental testbed, Alternate Configuration F pairs a Hyper-Assault Gauss 20 with three extended-range medium lasers. The HAG system represented cutting-edge Clan weapons technology when first mounted on the Nova, offering a burst-fire ballistic weapon that combined high damage potential with moderate range. This configuration reflects the Hell's Horses' continued investment in the Nova platform as a proving ground for new weapons systems.

Alternate Configuration G mounts a ProtoMech AC/8 with two tons of ammunition in the right arm, paired with an improved heavy medium laser in each side torso and seven extended-range small lasers in the left arm. All weapons are linked through a targeting computer, dramatically improving accuracy across the entire weapons suite. This configuration emphasizes precision engagement over raw firepower, making it particularly effective against hardened targets where every shot must count.

Developed by Clan Star Adder, Alternate Configuration H is one of the most feared Nova loadouts, mounting ten heavy medium lasers that can eviscerate most opponents at close range. Six additional double heat sinks provide some relief from the tremendous heat load, but the H configuration still runs dangerously hot during sustained fire. The heavy medium lasers' increased damage output compared to standard medium lasers makes this configuration devastating in short-range engagements, though it shares the Prime's vulnerability to overheating.

Alternate Configuration I combines an extended-range PPC in the right arm with five improved heavy medium lasers in the left arm, creating an asymmetric loadout effective at both long and short ranges. Five additional double heat sinks manage the considerable heat output from this energy-intensive weapons suite. The split between a single powerful long-range weapon and a cluster of short-range lasers demands careful tactical positioning to maximize both weapon systems simultaneously.

Alternate Configuration J pairs a Streak LRM-15 in the right arm with an extended-range PPC fitted with a PPC capacitor in the left arm. Two tons of missile ammunition sustain the Streak launcher's fire. The PPC capacitor allows the pilot to overcharge the particle cannon for increased damage at the cost of additional heat generation, providing a powerful alpha strike option against high-value targets. This configuration offers excellent standoff engagement capability with consistent accuracy from the Streak system.

Alternate Configuration K delivers long-range firepower through an extended-range large laser in the right arm and a Rotary Autocannon/2 in the left arm, fed by two tons of ammunition. Each side torso mounts an extended-range medium laser for supplementary fire. The RAC/2's rapid-fire capability provides sustained damage output at range, though the weapon's ammunition dependency and potential for jamming require the MechWarrior to balance aggression with caution during extended engagements.

Alternate Configuration L mounts an improved heavy large laser and a plasma cannon in each arm, creating a symmetrical loadout with devastating medium-range striking power. One ton of plasma ammunition in each side torso provides ten shots per cannon. The plasma cannons can both damage opponents and cause significant heat buildup in enemy units, making this configuration particularly effective against energy-dependent designs that already struggle with heat management.

The Primary configuration epitomizes the Nova's close-combat philosophy, mounting twelve extended-range medium lasers split evenly across both arms. Four additional double heat sinks supplement the chassis's base fourteen, though even eighteen sinks cannot fully manage the tremendous heat output of a full alpha strike. This configuration excels as a battle armor killer and close-range brawler, but demands exceptional heat management discipline from its MechWarrior to avoid potentially catastrophic shutdowns in sustained engagements.

Alternate Configuration R is a mixed-technology configuration incorporating Inner Sphere equipment alongside Clan systems. An engine supercharger allows brief bursts of increased speed, while the right arm mounts four medium re-engineered lasers and the left arm carries six anti-personnel Gauss rifles with two tons of ammunition. This unconventional loadout reflects the increasing technological exchange between Clan and Inner Sphere forces in the ilClan era, blending design philosophies in ways that would have been unthinkable in earlier centuries.

Alternate Configuration S is purpose-built for urban warfare, mounting six medium pulse lasers whose accuracy proves invaluable in the close confines of city fighting. Four machine guns provide effective anti-infantry capability, while an anti-missile system defends against the short-range missile attacks common in built-up areas. An active probe allows detection of hidden enemy units lurking in buildings or underground, making the S configuration a specialized but highly effective urban combat package.

Alternate Configuration T is a modern variation on the classic Prime loadout, mounting six medium chemical lasers and two tons of chemical laser ammunition in each arm. The chemical lasers offer comparable performance to standard medium lasers but rely on ammunition rather than pure energy output, fundamentally changing the Nova's traditional advantage of ammunition independence. This Tiburon Khanate-era configuration serves as a philosophical departure for the chassis while maintaining its signature close-range saturation fire doctrine.

Alternate Configuration U is an unusual specialized loadout designed to support boarding actions against enemy spacecraft. Two torso-mounted liquid storage tanks provide additional reaction mass for the jump jets, extending their operational endurance in zero-gravity environments. Eight machine guns and three heavy medium lasers handle anti-personnel and anti-armor duties respectively, while three micro pulse lasers provide precision fire. A light active probe and ECM suite provide electronic warfare capability, and a spot welder presumably facilitates hull breach repairs. Most remarkably, this configuration mounts a sword, marking one of the first instances of a Clan unit carrying a dedicated melee weapon.

Alternate Configuration X is an experimental loadout that pushes the boundaries of what the Nova chassis can accommodate. Drawing on prototype and advanced technologies, this configuration serves as a technology demonstrator and field trial platform. While details of its precise loadout remain limited compared to more established configurations, the X designation reflects its status as an experimental proof-of-concept rather than a standard production configuration intended for widespread deployment.

text.overview:
The Nova Cat is a 70-ton Clan heavy OmniMech introduced in 3059, commissioned by Khan Severen Leroux of Clan Nova Cat following the Clan's devastating defeat at the Battle of Tukayyid. Designed to rebuild both the touman's fighting strength and the Clan's shattered morale, the Nova Cat was christened after the Clan's spiritual namesake, imbuing it with deep symbolic significance for its warriors. The design draws heavy inspiration from Clan Jade Falcon's Night Gyr, trading five tons of mass for equivalent pod capacity through efficient use of an Endo Steel chassis and XL engine.

First produced at Barcella Alpha in Clan space, production expanded almost immediately to the Irece Alpha facility in the Inner Sphere. This dual-site manufacturing proved critical when Clan Nova Cat was abjured by the other Clans, ensuring uninterrupted production. The design's combination of heavy armor, generous pod space, and straightforward maintenance requirements made it popular well beyond its parent Clan, spreading rapidly to numerous other Clan and Inner Sphere factions over the following decades.
text.capabilities:
Long regarded as a pocket assault OmniMech, the Nova Cat sacrifices speed for firepower and protection. Its Consolidated Fusion 280 XL engine propels the seventy-ton chassis at a modest 43 kph cruising speed and 65 kph maximum, slower than most Clan heavies but sufficient for fire support and direct engagement roles. With over half its tonnage dedicated to weapons, ammunition, and equipment, the 38 tons of available pod space rivals many assault OmniMechs, giving technicians extraordinary flexibility in tailoring loadouts to mission requirements.

The Mynx Type Heavy Endo Steel frame supports 13.5 tons of Alpha Compound Plate armor, approaching the maximum protection possible for this weight class. Combined with a Clan XL engine that remains operational even after side torso loss, the Nova Cat is exceptionally difficult to destroy. Straightforward internal construction using common Clan components ensures rapid field repairs and reconfigurations, a significant logistical advantage for units operating far from supply lines.

The Primary configuration exemplifies the design's philosophy with two ER PPCs and three ER Large Lasers, creating a withering long-range energy barrage. Twenty-five double heat sinks struggle to dissipate a full alpha strike, but the all-energy loadout allows extended independent operations without ammunition concerns, and disciplined fire grouping keeps the 'Mech combat-effective indefinitely.
text.deployment: A Jihad-era development, the F configuration introduces six Improved Jump Jets that propel the Nova Cat up to one hundred and eighty meters in a single bound, granting exceptional tactical mobility for a heavy 'Mech. The weapons suite consists of two Large Pulse Lasers in the right arm and three Medium Pulse Lasers in the left, providing accurate fire at medium ranges. A targeting computer enhances weapon precision further, while an ECM Suite provides electronic warfare protection against guided munitions and sensor locks. Three additional double heat sinks manage the moderate thermal load. This configuration excels as a skirmisher, using its jump capability to seize advantageous positions while its ECM coverage supports lance-mates.
text.battleHistory:
The Nova Cat's origins are inseparable from the crisis that gripped Clan Nova Cat after Tukayyid. The Clan's defeat in 3052 shook its warriors to the core, and Khan Severen Leroux's decision to commission a new OmniMech was as much about restoring spiritual confidence as rebuilding military capability. Production began at Barcella Alpha, the Nova Cat capital world, and expanded to the Irece Alpha plant in early 3059 as the Clan began establishing its presence in the Inner Sphere.

The Nova Cat first saw significant combat during Operation Bulldog in 3059, when Clan Nova Cat's warriors turned their new OmniMech against Clan Smoke Jaguar. When the 357th Assault Cluster took Dyev from the Draconis Combine, the versatility of several Nova Cats proved decisive, with configurations mounting heavy autocannons and cluster munitions devastating militia vehicles and infantry formations. The sight of the towering twelve-meter 'Mech stalking through battlefield smoke became a potent psychological weapon against defending forces.

The Clan's Abjuration following their alliance with the Second Star League scattered Nova Cats across multiple factions' arsenals. Several units were seized by Clan Smoke Jaguar forces when they captured a malfunctioning Nova Cat DropShip during the chaos surrounding the Clan's dissolution. Sources in the Periphery persistently reported sightings of machines resembling the Nova Cat, suggesting that salvaged or captured examples may have entered the arsenals of Clans that accepted Smoke Jaguar refugees. The design also spread through more conventional channels, with Clan Diamond Shark's acquisition of the Barcella Alpha facility during the Civil War era enabling broader commercial distribution.

The Jihad proved devastating for Nova Cat production. The Irece Alpha plant was destroyed in 3071 during the Word of Blake's assault on the Draconis Combine, and individual Nova Cats were documented fighting desperate engagements against Blakist forces on worlds like Luthien and Caph. Despite the death of Clan Nova Cat as a political entity, the Tiburon Khanate maintained the Irece factory after it was rebuilt in the 3090s, meeting continued demand that proved both expected and surprising. Salvaged Nova Cats became a fixture in the Rasalhague Dominion, where native warriors of the former Free Rasalhague Republic put them to effective use despite being shunned by their Ghost Bear overlords.

By the ilClan era, the Nova Cat OmniMech had long outlived its parent Clan. Production continued at Irece under Draconis Combine control, while the Barcella facility's ownership passed through multiple Clan hands. Among the warriors of the Clan Protectorate, Nova Cat OmniMechs remain highly prized assets that frequently change hands through Trials of Possession, a fitting legacy for a design born from one Clan's determination to endure.

text.capabilities:
The OmniMarauder's fixed chassis serves as a masterwork of mixed-technology engineering. Built around a Clan-grade endo steel internal structure and powered by a Clan 300-rated extralight engine, the design achieves a respectable cruising speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour while leaving an impressive thirty-five and a half tons available for pod-mounted weaponry and equipment. Clan-manufactured double heat sinks provide efficient thermal management across all configurations. An Inner Sphere compact gyro further maximizes available space, a clever design choice that opens additional room in the torso sections for heavy armament. Sixteen and a half tons of ferro-lamellor armor provide exceptional protection, with the advanced armor's ability to reduce the impact of incoming fire giving the OmniMarauder survivability well beyond what standard armor of equivalent weight could offer.

The Primary configuration pays homage to the classic Marauder layout, mounting a Clan-grade extended-range PPC and extended-range medium laser in each arm alongside a devastating Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle 30 in the right torso. This combination of precision energy weapons and massive ballistic firepower gives the OmniMarauder tremendous damage potential at virtually all combat ranges. CASE II protects the MechWarrior from ammunition detonation, while five additional Clan double heat sinks supplement the chassis-mounted sinks to manage the considerable thermal load. The design's inherent quirks further enhance its battlefield presence, with a narrow and low-profile silhouette making it a difficult target, hyper-extending actuators providing superior firing arcs, and command-grade electronics supporting its role as a formation leader.

The OmniMarauder's greatest weakness is its near-total dependence on Clan-sourced components for every major structural system. This creates severe supply chain vulnerabilities that would make sustained frontline operations impractical, as battlefield damage to the chassis, engine, or armor would require Clan-manufactured replacements that cannot be sourced through standard Inner Sphere logistics networks.
text.deployment: The Primary Weapons Configuration deliberately echoes the weapon layout of the original MAD-3R Marauder, placing paired energy weapons in the arms with a heavy direct-fire weapon in the dorsal mount. The upgrade to Clan extended-range PPCs and medium lasers dramatically increases effective engagement range and damage output over the classic autocannon-and-PPC combination, while the Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle 30 replaces the original's autocannon with a weapon capable of devastating burst fire at medium ranges. Protected by CASE II and supported by seventeen double heat sinks, this configuration represents what the Marauder was always meant to be, a relentless direct-fire platform capable of breaking enemy formations through sheer weight of firepower.
text.battleHistory:
The OmniMarauder emerged from a period of significant investment in advanced 'Mech technology at General Motors' Kathil production complex. By the mid-thirty-second century, Kathil had become a center for cutting-edge beam weapon research, and the conventional Marauder had been firmly reestablished as a cornerstone of the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns' heavy 'Mech formations. Against this backdrop, GM leadership authorized a forward-looking feasibility study to determine whether the Marauder platform could be evolved into something truly revolutionary.

The decision to bring in an outside engineer from Bander BattleMechs proved crucial. The resulting design philosophy embraced Clan technology wholesale, prioritizing maximum capability over production economics to establish the upper boundary of what the Marauder lineage could achieve. The approach was deliberately extravagant, treating cost as no object in pursuit of a proof of concept.

The prototype's completion validated the concept technically but exposed the fundamental challenge of its economics. The sheer volume of Clan-sourced components, likely procured through Clan Sea Fox trading networks, drove per-unit costs to levels that made fleet procurement entirely impractical. The supply chain vulnerabilities inherent in relying on foreign-manufactured structural systems would also be unacceptable for a frontline combat asset in sustained operations.

Despite never entering production, the OmniMarauder served its intended purpose as a feasibility study. The lessons learned from its development informed subsequent Marauder upgrade programs and contributed to General Motors' growing expertise in mixed-technology integration. The prototype itself remains a sign of the enduring adaptability of the Marauder design, demonstrating that even after five centuries of service, the chassis continued to offer room for radical reinvention.

Each arm carries a plasma rifle with a ton of ammunition, weapons whose ability to generate crippling heat buildup in enemy 'Mechs remains unique to Inner Sphere arsenals. The centerpiece of the configuration is a massive Heavy Gauss Rifle split between the right and center torsos, delivering tremendous single-shot damage at long range. Clan CASE II in both torso locations shields the MechWarrior from the catastrophic consequences of the Heavy Gauss Rifle's volatile ammunition, while a Clan Light TAG provides target designation capability for supporting artillery or semi-guided munitions. This configuration trades the sustained firepower of the Prime for devastating alpha-strike potential.

text.overview: Commissioned by the Terran Hegemony in response to the expanding BattleMech arms race that followed Operation PROMETHEUS, the Orion was designed by General Mechanics on Mars as the Hegemony’s premier heavy attack BattleMech. First fielded in prototype form in 2456, the seventy-five-ton design has remained in continuous production for over half a millennium, making it one of the longest-serving BattleMech designs in history. Often called “a poor man’s Atlas,” the Orion earned lasting fame as the chosen mount of General Aleksandr Kerensky during his campaign to liberate Terra from Stefan Amaris, an image that made the Orion one of the most recognized BattleMechs in known space. Production shifted to Kali Yama Weapons Industries in the Free Worlds League after the fall of the Star League, and the Orion’s roomy, easily maintained chassis has proven remarkably adaptable to successive generations of weapons technology, ensuring its continued relevance across every major conflict of the last five centuries.
text.capabilities:
The Orion’s design philosophy emphasizes versatility through a balanced mix of ballistic, missile, and energy weapons systems, an approach that has kept the chassis competitive even as battlefield technology has evolved dramatically. The standard ON1-K mounts a KaliYama Class 10 Autocannon as its primary weapon, supplemented by a KaliYama Death Bloom LRM-15 launcher for ranged fire support, two Irian Weapons Works medium lasers, and an SRM-4 rack to exploit armor breaches at close range. Over fourteen tons of Valiant Lamellor armor provides protection sufficient for sustained frontline combat, while a Vlar 300 fusion engine delivers a respectable maximum speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour.

The chassis’s greatest strength lies in its adaptability. The roomy internal layout has readily accommodated every major technological advancement since the Star League era, from XL engines and double heat sinks to extended-range weaponry and advanced fire control systems. This flexibility has produced an extraordinary number of variants, from simple field refits that swap missile launchers to ground-up redesigns mounting Gauss rifles and experimental weapons. Any MechWarrior who can pilot one Orion can quickly adapt to virtually any variant, a logistical advantage that few other designs can match.
text.deployment: When Clan Wolf captured the Kali Yama production facilities on Kalidasa, they resurrected the Orion as a successor to the Orion IIC, a fitting tribute to Kerensky’s legacy from the Clan that claims guardianship of it. Built on the ON2-M’s endo steel frame, the Orion C hides beneath thick ferro-lamellor armor and mounts Streak LRM-15s, ER pulse lasers, a Gauss rifle, and CASE II protection, cutting-edge Clan technology throughout. While some Wolf warriors question using non-Clan structural components, the decision to leverage existing manufacturing infrastructure reduced the strain on the Wolves’ industrial resources.
text.battleHistory:
The Orion’s origins trace to the earliest days of the BattleMech arms race. After the Lyran Commonwealth obtained BattleMech technology through Operation PROMETHEUS, the Terran Hegemony commissioned General Mechanics of Mars to develop a new heavy attack ’Mech. The first ON1-C prototype debuted in 2453 but was rejected by the Hegemony Armed Forces for insufficient firepower. General Mechanics returned to the drawing board, settling on a smaller engine to free mass for additional weapons. The third prototype (the ON1-H, incorporating the newly developed class-10 autocannon) finally won HAF approval in 2456.

The Orion served the Hegemony with distinction, but its defining moment came centuries later during the Amaris Civil War. General Aleksandr Kerensky chose an Orion as his personal BattleMech, piloting it through the liberation of Terra and the capture of Stefan Amaris. That olive-drab Orion became one of the most recognized machines in military history. When Kerensky departed on the Exodus, he abandoned the venerable ’Mech, which was eventually recovered by Combine salvage teams in the New Samarkand system and given to the young Theodore Kurita. Named “Revenant,” the machine served Theodore through the Fourth Succession War before reportedly being destroyed on Marfik.

Production shifted from the original Hesperus II and Mars facilities to Kali Yama Weapons Industries on Kalidasa and the Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation joint venture on Kendall following the fall of the Star League. The Free Worlds League became the largest producer, fueling complaints that the Marik Militia received more than their fair share of new Orions. The Outreach Accords during the Clan Invasion opened League military exports to the other Great Houses, sparking a golden age for Kali Yama and the Alphard Trading Corporation.

The recovery of Star League technology in the late 3040s produced the ON1-M upgrade, trading the temperamental autocannon for a versatile LB 10-X and adding an XL engine. The plethora of field variants that followed (Artemis IV refits, MRM conversions, rotary autocannon upgrades, and light Gauss substitutions) testified to the chassis’s enduring adaptability. The ON2-M represented the first ground-up redesign, employing an endo steel frame, Gauss rifle, and Artemis-equipped LRM-15 to create what many consider the definitive modern Orion. Kali Yama’s ON3-M “Orion 3100” pushed the design further with Extended LRM technology, though declining military budgets limited initial sales.

When Clan Wolf captured Kalidasa, they converted the Kali Yama production lines to build the Orion C, a fitting tribute to Kerensky’s legacy that combined the proven Inner Sphere chassis with cutting-edge Clan weaponry.

text.overview: The Orion has long held an important place in the Clan Wolf Touman, and the Orion C 2 is a capable heir to the favored ride of Aleksandr Kerensky. The response has been mixed, however, as it continues to use non-Clan structural components to reduce the strain on the Wolves’ industrial resources. The weapons, though, are mostly Clan. Short to medium range is covered by a Streak rack and ER medium laser, backed up with a large pulse laser in the left arm. The Orion’s standard right torso ballistic weapon was replaced by an ER large laser, both for weight and range. Having been burned by the superior range of extended LRMs, the Wolves are experimenting with the weapon system on the C 2.
text.notableUnits: Captain Phil “Wonderdog” Dalbeck: A MechWarrior in mercenary Helmut’s Legion, Dalbeck obtained his Orion C 2 through suicidal bravery. Regarding his ultra-short ranged Spider SDR-9M to be a death trap, he sought less risky scouting assignments. However, upon spotting a damaged Orion C 2 leading a solahma Star during a deep raid on Uzhgorod, “Wonderdog” exploited zellbrigen to duel the Orion in single combat in rough terrain. He saw in the Orion a chance for advancement and long-term survival, so he pushed his Spider to its limits dodging fire while hitting the thinner rear armor of the Orion. Luck favored him when he decapitated the Orion’s artillery-damaged head. Dalbeck was later assigned the salvaged Orion, though he frequently notes that the bureaucratic battle to claim the ’Mech was harder than the actual battle.
